To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of reception diversity and the L PPM modulation scheme, instead of the conventional OOK, are both very effective means to enhance the TOW system availability, in terms of BER, in the presence of the combined impact of the skin induced attenuation and the pointing error effect.

(i) The outage performance of the total TOWER system can be significantly improved by using reception diversity schemes along with L PPM modulation format, (ii) the employment of reception diversity schemes can compensate for the degradation in outage performance that is caused by pointing errors, and (iii) the outage performance of the TOW system can be further improved by increasing the number of the employed receivers.

the proposed reception diversity TOW systems are able to improve significantly the average BER performance of a single receiver configuration in the presence of both skin induced attenuation and pointing error effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the outage performance of TOW links in the presence of skin induced attenuation, pointing errors, and reception diversity configurations.
the performance of SIMO TOW links with multiple receivers in the presence of skin induced attenuation, and pointing errors.

the analysis of the outage performance of a novel TOW link that is capable to operate in the presence of strong attenuation and pointing errors, and is based on the employment of reception diversity configurations and L PPM schemes for data transmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed reception diversity system with L PPM modulation scheme is able to provide a considerable performance improvement over the conventional OOK modulation scheme in a TOW link.

the proposed TOW reception diversity configurations can be used to improve the system performance, in terms of average BER and outage probability, by increasing the number of receivers, as well as by using more power effective modulation schemes, such as L PPM.
the proposed SIMO reception diversity configuration, combined with the more power effective LPPM scheme, is the optimal choice in order to achieve the best possible TOW link availability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the employment of the L PPM modulation scheme along with reception diversity configurations is a promising solution for enhancing the TOW system availability, especially for the case of large values of the boresight pointing error.

the proposed SIMO TOW system with L PPM is more energy efficient than the conventional OOK, and that reception diversity configurations can be employed for enhancing TOW availability in the presence of pointing errors and strong skin attenuation.
the proposed reception diversity system with the use of LPPM modulation scheme, outperforms the OOK based one, in all considered cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the same average optical power, reception diversity configurations are more effective in terms of outage performance than the single receiver configuration.
the proposed TOW system with reception diversity can provide considerable improvements in terms of BER performance compared to a non diversity configuration.
, by using a suitable modulation format, the outage probability of the TOW link can be reduced significantly.
